summary: Autonomous UV-C disinfection robot for healthcare and shared facilities.
editor_note: Violet makes disinfection a mapped, repeatable robot workflow instead of a manually positioned lamp. It navigates without pre-mapping, detects high-touch objects, shuts its lamps off when a person enters, and generates coverage reports for compliance. The product is unusually inspectable for a young robotics company. Its hardest test is whether facility deployments reproduce the lab and company-reported pathogen reductions.

product_evidence.claim: The Violet Gen4 page shows autonomous navigation without pre-mapping, high-touch-object detection, person-triggered lamp shutoff, and mobile coverage reporting.
The official product surface specifies eight UV-C lamps, selectable disinfection cycles, replaceable components, and downloadable room-cleaning reports.
The company-issued financing announcement attributes the round to an unnamed investment entity associated with Agadia Systems; it does not establish Agadia Systems itself as the lead investor.

market_context.primary_user: Hospitals, senior-care facilities, schools, laboratories, hotels, and other operators with repeatable room-disinfection workflows.
market_context.differentiation: Autonomous navigation and object-aware UV-C coverage with an auditable room report.
market_context.why_now: Facilities face labor constraints and infection-control requirements that favor repeatable automation with visible safety controls.

risks.claim: The open question is whether field deployments reproduce company-reported microbial reduction and room-turnover benefits across varied layouts.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment based on the official product page and company-issued financing release.
